name: Overhead
short: Scroll to climb — the valley draws itself in contours as you rise.
long: The page is an ascent. Scrolling is altitude: the telemetry counts up, a fictional Peak District dale inks itself in from the valley floor to the tops, and by 120 m the whole view has tilted from an oblique into a flat survey sheet. The map is generated in the browser from one height field, so the contours, the dry-stone walls, the hedgerows and the brook all come out of the same arithmetic.
proves: A survey outfit can show what it actually hands over instead of a gallery of aerial photos.
features: Scroll is altitude — the contour map draws itself in as the aircraft climbs
Telemetry pinned at the top: altitude, a moving heading tape, wind and battery
At the top the view tilts from oblique through to a full plan-view sheet
Services as a real flight log; hover a job and its contour band lights up on the keymap
A picker rewrites the log for a roof, a site, land or a property to sell
Before and after roof: the frame as flown against a measurable orthomosaic, with a draggable divider
Enquiry form takes a postcode and returns a draft flight plan
story: Drone operators all show the same thing — a gallery of pretty aerial photographs. What they are actually paid for is measurement, so this page is built out of a map that measures itself, and the roof survey is shown twice: once as a picture, once as something you can put a tape to.
